title: Austin: Waterfront Plans, New Paving & Elections
summary:
*   **Lake Austin Recreation:** Approved a petition for private citizens to build a gasoline-powered steam launch on Lake Austin, utilizing overflow land near the dam.
*   **Major Infrastructure Push:** Discussed plans for extensive Bitulithic street paving across the city, awarded a contract for a new culvert, and began the process of appropriating $250,000 in sewer bonds for city improvements.
*   **Investing in City Growth:** Transferred $42,500 for bond redemption and approved funds to purchase land for widening and extending city streets.
*   **Election Readiness:** Appointed numerous judges and clerks across all seven city wards to oversee elections for the next two years.

Feby 25th,1913,
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin : That the bid of A A Mundt to build the reinforced concrete culvert across
Waller Creek at about the intersection of 11th & Red River streets for the price of $
4,492.00, be and the same is hereby accepted.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City
Council of the City of Austin : That two hundred ($ 200.00) dollars out of the general
contingent fundbe and the same is hereby set apart and appropriated to pay Messrs L N
Goldbeck and Herman Pressler for the conveyance to the City of Austin for street purposes
of a strip of land of varying width from twenty one(21') feet to nine and ahalf feet (9½')
and six hundred and sixty four feet (664') long on the west side of a tract of about seven
(7) acres recently purchased by them of Thomas Spence of this City ,and coming up for its
western line to East Avenue; and for the further conveyance to the City of Austnfor street
purposes of a strip of land varying from seventeen (17') feet to nineteen (19') feet in
width by four hundred ,fifty and and five tenths feet ( 450 5/10) in length on the south
side of said Spence property, to be a part of Holly street in this City.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
